prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the depth map captures the camera wearer stepping from a hallway into a small pantry alcove (frames 1 to 3) and then turning left to exit back down the hallway (frames 4 to 5), with no other people truly present in the scene. In frames 2 and 3, bright white regions show a wire shelving unit on the right within arm's reach at roughly 0.3–0.6 m, stocked with jars and boxes on an upper and lower tier that partially occlude containers behind them, while a medium-grey stack of white bags topped with a red object sits on the floor in the back-left corner about 1.0–1.2 m away and roughly 0.5 m to the left of and behind the shelf. In frames 1, 4, and 5, bright vertical bands mark the nearby doorway wall and frame within arm's reach at 0.3–0.6 m, contrasting with dark receding hallways and closed wooden doors on the left at 1.5–3.0 m and a distant room 4–6 m away in frame 5. The depth map clarifies 3D surface separation and recess distances that are hard to judge in the motion-blurred, uniformly yellow-lit RGB frames, such as the exact step-back between the protruding doorframe and the hallway door behind it. However, the map is unreliable in maintaining consistent scale across frames—the corner wall behind the bags looks much darker and farther in frame 3 than in frames 2 and 4 due to per-frame normalization when the shelf is very close—and it blurs across the thin wire shelf grates.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map highlights objects only in frames 2, 3, and 4 as the camera wearer turns into and out of the pantry alcove, labeling a vertical form on the left (~1.0–1.2 m away) as a 'person' and three items on the right-hand shelf in frame 3 (~0.3–0.5 m away, within arm's reach) as 'bottle'. In frame 3, the three 'bottle' masks sit about 0.5 m to the right of and slightly above the base of the 'person' mask, showing two foreground jars in front of and partially occluding a narrower middle container between them, while the rest of the shelf is cut off at the right and bottom frame edges. Across frames 2 to 4, the 'person' mask shifts from the lower-left edge to the center-left and then to the lower-right as the camera wearer approaches the shelf and then turns left to retreat into the hallway. While the masks in frame 3 help isolate individual foreground containers from the cluttered, overlapping pantry items in the RGB image, the segmentation map is largely unreliable in its semantic labels and coverage. Comparison with the RGB strip reveals that the segmented 'person' is actually an inanimate stack of white plastic bags topped with a dark red item (so there is no person facing or looking anywhere), the 'bottle' masks misclassify wide peanut-butter jars and a rectangular box, and all surrounding shelves, doors, and containers in frames 1–5 are completely missed.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, and contains only a single small yellow body skeleton with no magenta hand keypoints in the lower-center of frame 4 as the camera wearer turns left to leave the alcove. This skeleton places a cluster of head keypoints above a trapezoidal torso at roughly 1.0–1.2 m from the camera wearer (just beyond arm's reach), positioned to the right of the doorway edge and to the left of the partly cropped wire shelf at the far right edge. Based on the symmetrical shoulder line and facial keypoint cluster alone, the detected figure would appear to have its torso angled toward the camera wearer with its lower body occluded below the frame edge, and no objects within its reach except the adjacent wall. While a pose map would ordinarily reveal body orientation under dim lighting, comparison with the RGB strip shows that no person exists in the scene at all. The detection in frame 4 is a false positive triggered by the stack of white plastic bags topped with a red cloth in the corner, making the pose map entirely unreliable here.
